name: Neo-kitsch
overall: A close recreation. Layout, proportions, the wire bands, the cascade cards and the weapon art register almost one-to-one, and at thumbnail size the two are hard to tell apart. Up close, the dark lettering on gold surfaces gives it away: the ENTER/LOGIN bars, the dashboard EMAIL panel and the selected store card set their text pale, thin and widely spaced, where the reference uses a firm dark brown. The wood veneer is the second giveaway: ours is evenly spaced straight stripes, the reference is figured grain with a seam and a bevelled rim.

screens.name: Login
screens.verdict: The composition matches almost exactly; the two ENTER / LOGIN bars are the one thing that reads wrong at a glance.
matches: ARASAKA logotype, its info box, the clock block and both PRASE fields sit where the reference has them, at the right size.
The bottom wire band, with its plateaus and mirrored S-bend rises onto a single bridging line, matches in shape and strand count.
The A and B badges, the fine print beside them and the bottom disclaimer line are placed and sized right.

gaps.t: ENTER / LOGIN bars: the reference label is a compact, dark-grey, wide geometric face with normal spacing. Ours is thin, very pale and letter-spaced across the whole bar, so it almost vanishes.
gaps.ref: NK-05; the notes say the CTA was deliberately left unchanged

gaps.t: Input fields: the reference fill is a warm maroon-brown. Ours is a duller, greyer brown.
ENTER / LOGIN bars: the reference's right end has slightly rounded corners; ours is square-cut.
Violet glow at the top: ours spreads further right and leaves a teal cast in the top-right corner, where the reference fades to near-black.
Small type under the logotype uses a squarer, pixel-like face, and its S reads almost like a 6 or G. The logotype's edges look slightly stair-stepped at 3x zoom.

screens.name: Mailbox
screens.verdict: The strongest of the four: the list, the message body, the RIFLES buttons and the header band all line up, and only the selected row and the right-hand header labels read differently.
matches: The seven mail rows, their envelope icons, underlines and tabs, and the wording and line breaks are at the reference positions.
The message body matches in font, size, line breaks and hyphenation.
The header wire band, the A/B badges and the T2 wireframe badge closely follow the reference.
The four RIFLES buttons match in size, spacing, corner cut and label.

gaps.t: Selected row ("Urgent information"): the reference veneer has wavy, figured grain, a vertical seam near FROM: MOM, a darker bevelled rim and a rounded, tapered right end. Ours is flat, regular wavy stripes with a hard right cut. A row of small scallops also runs along its top edge, which the reference does not have.

Top-right header: SECURITY LEVEL and the LEVEL/T1, T3 and T4 labels sit about 8px higher than LEVEL/T2 inside the badge. In the reference all share one baseline. The dashboard header has them aligned, so this is specific to the mailbox.
Top-right header: the T1-T4 numerals are narrower and heavier than the reference's wider, squarer letters.
Selected row text is a little paler than the reference's dark brown.

screens.name: Store
screens.verdict: The structure, card geometry and weapon art are excellent; the selected card's text, the product-name lines and the BASKET panel are what separate it from the reference.
matches: 4ST STORE logotype, the customer/discount block, the left nav buttons (SMG selected) and the header wire band all match.
The four product cards match in stepped tops, stacked echo outlines, foot tabs, stat grid and socket cells. The MAGNUM weapon drawings are very faithful.
The selected centre card's layout (stats, Recoil/Spread/Range, Bonus lines, socket row) is in the right places.

gaps.t: Selected centre card: the body text (Recoil, Spread, Bonus) is thin and pale in ours, and starts about 10px further left. The reference is a medium-weight dark brown and clearly legible.
Selected centre card: the reference veneer has a strong horizontal figured streak through the middle and warm darker shading. Ours is pale, even grain with one faint line.

BASKET panel (top right): our fine print is larger than the reference's, so it runs out of the panel and is clipped ("ARE", "DEVIC"). The reference panel also has visible grain and a seam; ours is a flat fill.
MAGNUM 650 HAND GUN on all cards: ours is centred about 10px left of the reference, and "HAND GUN" is lighter and wider-spaced than the reference's medium weight.
Card outlines: the outer echo strokes are crisper and more uniform than the reference's graded bright-to-faint stack.

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.verdict: The cascade cards and header are spot on, but the gold EMAIL preview panel on the right, the screen's focal point, has nearly unreadable body text and plain grain.
matches: The six module cards match in staggered placement, the chamfer plus diagonal foot, stacked echo lines and label tabs.
The header (CUSTOMER, LEVEL T1, the SECURITY LEVEL row aligned correctly here, the wire band) and the C/D footers match.
The right panel's outline, its stepped top and the EMAIL caption below it are right.

gaps.t: Right EMAIL panel body: ours is thin, pale and letter-spaced, barely darker than the gold. The reference is a dark-brown medium weight that reads easily. The biggest single visual miss on the screen.
gaps.ref: likely NK-05, not called out for this panel

gaps.t: Selected EMAIL cascade card: the reference grain converges into a horizontal book-match seam about halfway down and has a thin bevelled gold rim. Ours is straight, evenly spaced vertical stripes with no rim.
Right panel veneer: the reference has a curved wood figure in the lower third and darker shading at the top and bottom edges. Ours is nearly uniform.
Header A/B fine print: the B note in ours is right-aligned against the badge, while the reference's is left-aligned. Ours is also wider-spaced.
Fine-print blocks under the cards are slightly bolder and squarer than the reference. Hard to judge at this size.

screens.question: The flat, straight-stripe veneer has been the slowest item to converge (many rejected fits are recorded). Would you accept a pre-rendered raster texture for the selected wood surfaces, as the era's own notes suggest, instead of drawing the grain as vector lines?
